children: ), a leading independent energy company with over 20 years of successful operations across Latin America, reports its consolidated financial results for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026 (“Third Quarter” or “3Q2026”). A conference call to discuss these results will be held on November 4, 2026, at 8:00 am (Eastern Standard Time).

During 3Q2026, GeoPark delivered stable production from its Colombian assets and accelerated production growth in Vaca Muerta, Argentina. The Company also announced its strategic entry into Venezuela through the Bare Block, a large-scale heavy oil redevelopment opportunity in the Orinoco Oil Belt. Financial performance was primarily impacted by wider crude oil differentials and higher operating costs. Following quarter-end, GeoPark strengthened its growth platform through the award of the Corralera Noreste Block in Argentina and secured long-term funding through a $550 million senior notes issuance to enhance its financial profile and support its Vaca Muerta investment program. Full-year 2026 results are expected to remain within market guidance, supported by increasing production volumes in Argentina and Colombia and optimizing fourth-quarter hedge positions to mitigate the impact of weaker crude oil differentials.
All figures are expressed in US Dollars and comparisons refer to 2Q2026, except when specified.

Brent prices averaged $91.4/bbl during the quarter, compared to $96.9/bbl in 2Q2026. Significantly wider crude oil differentials further pressured GeoPark’s realized pricing. In Colombia, the Vasconia differential widened to a discount of $6.67/bbl from $1.43/bbl, while in Argentina, the Medanito differential deteriorated to a discount of $3.50/bbl from a premium of $1.79/bbl. Combined realized prices, including the impact of existing commodity risk management contracts, fell to $56.2/boe in 3Q2026, compared to $67.2/boe.

Production from Colombia and Argentina averaged 27,973 boepd, up 3% compared to 2Q2026, supported by stable production in Colombia and a 51% increase in Argentina. Nonetheless, sales volumes1 decreased by 4% compared to 2Q2026, reflecting the absence of incremental pipeline inventory sales recorded in the previous quarter. Altogether, revenue decreased by 19% to $116.2 million in 3Q2026.

Capital expenditures totaled $72.2 million, one of GeoPark’s highest quarterly investment levels in recent years, bringing investment over the past two quarters to $148.6 million. The Vaca Muerta program is progressing ahead of the original development schedule, bringing forward investment and expected production growth. ROACE as of 3Q2026 stands at 17%.

Adjusted EBITDA2 totaled $45.8 million (39% margin), down 37%. The decrease primarily reflected lower realized oil prices and higher operating costs, which increased to $20.7 per produced boe from $17.9 per produced boe, mainly driven by higher energy costs, increased well intervention activities and the appreciation of the Colombian and Argentine currencies3. These factors were partially offset by higher production and a lower negative impact from commodity risk management contracts. LTM Adjusted EBITDA4 is $236.5 million.

GeoPark continues to manage its hedging portfolio to protect downside exposure and support cash flow predictability. In 3Q2026, revenue reflected a $36.4 million loss from commodity risk management contracts, compared to a $41.2 million loss, as Brent prices remained above the contracted price ceilings. The Company continues to optimize its hedging portfolio, including the rollover of 6,000 bopd of existing 4Q2026 hedges into a 2028 position, while replacing the original 4Q2026 hedges with zero-cost collars at improved price levels. As a result, the hedge position is 25,000 boepd in 4Q2026, with average floors of $69 per boe and price ceilings of $79 per boe.

GeoPark generated $16.3 million of cash flow from operating activities during the quarter, compared to $108.4 million in 2Q2026, reflecting lower operating profitability and working capital movements, primarily driven by higher accounts receivable in Argentina, increased inventories in Colombia and other advances and receivables. Free cash flow before debt service stood at negative $55.5 million. The shift to negative free cash flow in 3Q2026 is consistent with the anticipated investment phase of GeoPark’s Vaca Muerta development. The dividend suspension announced in October 2025, effective with the 3Q2026 results, was designed to preserve cash through this phase.

Notwithstanding the above, cash and cash equivalents stood at $253.4 million at the end of 3Q2026, compared to $316.3 million in 2Q2026. Net debt stood at $386.6 million, with a net leverage ratio of 1.6x, compared to $317.8 million and 1.2x, respectively, at the end of 2Q2026.

Operating profit stood at $11.6 million in 3Q2026, compared to $40.8 million. Net income for the quarter totaled $6.6 million, including a $12.4 million income tax benefit, primarily resulting from deferred income tax adjustments in Argentina.

Subsequent to quarter-end, GeoPark completed a $550 million offering of 9.500% senior notes due 2033, strengthening its debt maturity profile and financial flexibility. As part of the transaction, approximately $266.8 million, representing 60% of the outstanding 2030 Notes were repurchased, while the proceeds also supported the redemption of the 2027 Notes. The transaction reduces near-term refinancing risk and funds a substantial portion of the Company’s planned 2027 investment program in Vaca Muerta.

During 3Q2026, GeoPark announced its strategic entry into Venezuela through the Bare Block, a large-scale heavy oil redevelopment opportunity in the Orinoco Oil Belt. On November 2, 2026, the Company completed the transaction, with the 25-year Production Participation Contract (“CPP”) becoming effective following the fulfillment of all required contractual and regulatory milestones. GeoPark is now advancing preparations to assume operational control before year-end 2026, with initial activities focused on well reactivations, production stabilization and infrastructure rehabilitation.

In October 2026, GeoPark was awarded the Corralera Noreste Block in northern Vaca Muerta, Argentina, adding approximately 26,900 gross acres (24,200 acres net to GeoPark’s 90% working interest). Based on its current technical assessment, the block has approximately 200 mmboe of unrisked gross resource potential and potential gross peak production of 40,000–50,000 boepd, subject to successful appraisal and development. GeoPark will pursue a phased de-risking strategy, with further investments subject to technical performance and investment criteria, while initial commitments are expected to be funded with available cash.

Felipe Bayon, Chief Executive Officer of GeoPark, said: “Our third-quarter results reflect the ongoing portfolio transition from harvesting cash from mature assets to disciplined investment in transformational long-term growth. While key strategic milestones were achieved through the signing of the Bare agreement in Venezuela and the acquisition of new acreage in Argentina, wider crude oil differentials and higher operating costs are challenging current margins, reinforcing our focus on efficiency, proactive balance sheet management, and disciplined capital allocation. With the recent refinancing of our debt underpinning our development plans, our priority is to excel in execution, converting investment into production and cash flow growth while preserving financial strength.”

Operating Netback is equivalent to Adjusted EBITDA net of cash expenses included in Administrative, Geological and Geophysical and Other operating costs

ROACE is defined as last twelve-month operating profit divided by average capital employed. Capital employed is calculated as total assets minus current liabilities and adjusted for excess cash. Excess cash corresponds to the portion of cash and cash equivalents that exceeds the amount required to cover current liabilities with current assets.

The Company believes Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and operating netback per boe, which are each non-GAAP measures, are useful because they allow the Company to more effectively evaluate its operating performance and compare the results of its operations from period to period without regard to its financing methods or capital structure. The Company’s calculation of Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, and operating netback per boe may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies.

The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA as profit for the period before net finance costs, income tax, depreciation, amortization and certain non-cash items such as impairments and write-offs of unsuccessful exploration and evaluation assets, accrual of stock options and stock awards, unrealized results on commodity risk management contracts and other non-recurring events. Adjusted EBITDA is not a measure of profit or cash flow as determined by IFRS. The Company excludes the items listed above from profit for the period in arriving at Adjusted EBITDA because these amounts can vary substantially from company to company within its industry depending upon accounting methods and book values of assets, capital structures and the method by which the assets were acquired. Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to, or more meaningful than, profit for the period or cash flow from operating activities as determined in accordance with IFRS or as an indicator of its operating performance or liquidity. Certain items excluded from Adjusted EBITDA are significant components in understanding and assessing a company’s financial performance, such as a company’s cost of capital and tax structure and significant and/or recurring write-offs, as well as the historic costs of depreciable assets, none of which are components of Adjusted EBITDA. For a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to the IFRS financial measure of profit, see the accompanying financial tables and the supplementary information.
